subject: Reserved Dedicated term structure and capacity kickoff - ClearWave Health
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Ramos <julia@clearwavehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwavehealth.com
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Reserved Dedicated term structure and capacity kickoff - ClearWave Health

Julia — thanks again for the time this morning. Attached is a first-pass term sheet for the Dedicated reserved commit options we discussed (12/24/36 months) and a short FAQ that summarizes how we handle ramp windows and capacity start dates.

Key items I want to call out up front:
- We support 3 commit terms: 12 / 24 / 36 months. Each has a different discount ladder tied to committed GPU-hours and sustained throughput.
- Standard ramp window is 90 days from the start date with a 100% credit for unmet committed units during the ramp. We can discuss shortening or phasing the ramp.
- We offer a small onboarding credit for larger commits (applies to invoice credit, not a rebate).

Can you confirm:
1) Your preferred term length (you mentioned procurement was leaning toward something shorter for budgeting)
2) Target capacity start date range (end of Q2 vs. earlier)
3) Any internal SLOs we should reflect in the term sheet (e.g., 99th pct latency or throughput targets)

I've attached: Redwood_Dedicated_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (term sheet) and ClearWave_RFP_Qs.pdf (your RFP with our inline answers).

Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to run through the options live.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0198

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (PDF, 24 pages), ClearWave_RFP_Qs.pdf (PDF, 8 pages)

From: Julia Ramos <julia@clearwavehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@clearwavehealth.com, Matt Hendrix <matt.hendrix@procurex.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved Dedicated term structure and capacity kickoff - ClearWave Health

Vanessa — appreciate the docset. A few quick clarifications from procurement and our cloud infra team: 

- Term length: our finance team prefers 12 or 24 months to avoid 3-year lock-in. If the delta in discount between 24 and 36 months is material, we could consider 24.
- Start date: ideal is July 1, 2026, but we may be able to push to June 1 if onboarding is lightweight.
- Ramp: procurement asked whether Redwood can support a staged start where 50% of committed capacity becomes available at contract start, with the remainder phased in over 3 months. They also asked if there's a cap on how long we can extend the ramp before discounts change.
- SLA/throughput: our product team will ask for a 99% throughput availability target for the committed pool and wants a clear fall-back for degraded performance (e.g., automatic routing to hosted instances plus credit for degraded intervals).

Matt from ProcureX is copied — he will help us evaluate commercial tradeoffs. Can you confirm whether Redwood can: (A) accept a 50%-then-phased ramp, (B) provide SLA language for throughput availability, and (C) offer a one-time onboarding credit or reduced TCV in the first invoice?

Thanks,
Julia Ramos
Head of AI Platforms, ClearWave Health

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Ramos <julia@clearwavehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwavehealth.com, Matt Hendrix <matt.hendrix@procurex.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 14:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved Dedicated term structure and capacity kickoff - ClearWave Health

Julia — short answers inline below, then a short proposal: 

A) 50% initial capacity with phased remainder: YES. We routinely do a phased start. Typical pattern we propose is: 50% capacity active at contract start, 75% by day 60, 100% by day 180. We can shorten to full availability by day 90 for modest concession on discount (I outline options in the attached term sheet).

B) SLA / throughput language: YES. We can commit to an availability SLO for the reserved pool (measured as % of requested token throughput served from the dedicated pool) with credits for missed targets. We prefer to define the SLO around sustained throughput and 99th percentile latency for inference requests above baseline batch sizes. The legal team prefers credit caps (monthly credit capped at X% of monthly committed ARR) — I included sample language in v2.

C) One-time onboarding credit: YES. For a mid-sized 24-month commit we can offer a one-time $45,000 onboarding credit to offset integration and migration costs. For 12-month terms the credit is smaller ($20,000) and for 36-month terms we can increase it to $60,000. Credits are applied as invoice credits over month 1-3.

Short proposal (what I'll mark in the term sheet if we move forward):
- Term: 24 months (preferred by Redwood for balance of churn and price)
- Committed pool size: 12 A100-equivalent GPUs (we'll size final pool after you share usage profiles)
- Start window: contract signature -> initial 50% capacity on Day 1; 75% by Day 60; 100% by Day 180 (we can accelerate to Day 90 for +2% discount on TCV)
- Discount: 22% off hosted list pricing for 24m baseline (sliding scale +/- 3% depending on final sizing)
- Onboarding credit: $45,000 applied across first 3 invoices
- SLA: 99% throughput availability SLO (sample credit schedule in v2)

I've attached an updated term sheet that highlights the 24m proposal and an appendix with SLO sample language. Also attaching forecast_impact.xlsx — a quick sensitivity that shows how different ramps affect Redwood unit economics.

If that looks close, I'll push a clean term sheet to DocuSign and we can route it to your procurement for approval.

Best,
Vanessa

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (updated), forecast_impact.xlsx (XLSX, 3 sheets)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: ClearWave commercial — margin impact and ask for approval

Markus / Karthik — copying the proposal I'm about to send to ClearWave (summary below). Need quick approval on two commercial levers before I lock the sheet: 

Summary of external ask/proposal: 24m term, 12 A100-eq GPUs committed, 50% initial capacity at Day 0, ramp to 100% by Day 180 (option to accelerate to Day 90 for -2% TCV). Discount at 22%, one-time onboarding credit $45k.

Questions for you: 
1) Can legal cap acceptable ramp extension to +60 days beyond the standard schedule? Procurement is evaluating a staged start and wants flexibility.
2) Can finance accept a $45k onboarding credit for a mid-size commit (internal expected ARR ~ $1.8M/year post-discount)?
3) Any region-specific constraints — ClearWave will run in us-west (they confirmed offline). If we need to reserve physical hosts in a single region, what's the allocation impact?

Attached is forecast_impact.xlsx with breakouts if they accelerate vs. decelerate the ramp. I can push the draft to DocuSign when we have the thumbs-up.

Thanks,
Vanessa

Attachments: forecast_impact.xlsx (XLSX, 3 sheets)

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: ClearWave commercial — margin impact and ask for approval

Vanessa — fine to proceed with external proposal with the following guardrails: 
- Legal: allow a maximum ramp extension of 60 days beyond the standard schedule (i.e., 50% Day 0, 75% Day 60, 100% Day 180 + up to 60 days extension). We should not allow open-ended ramp slack that meaningfully defers the TCV recognition.
- Finance: onboarding credit $45k is acceptable for a $1.8M ARR profile; ensure credit is explicitly invoiced as a negative line item over months 1-3 so ARR math is clean.
- Ops: since ClearWave will be us-west, we should reserve A100-equivalent capacity in us-west2; ops team confirms this is available but will require a 4-week lead time to pin instances on the infra side. Add a note in the term sheet about the 30-day operational lead.

Markus
VP, Commercial Strategy

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Ramos <julia@clearwavehealth.com>, procurement@clearwavehealth.com, Matt Hendrix <matt.hendrix@procurex.com>

Julia / team — thanks for the patience while we finalized internal approvals. Per our internal confirmation and your asks, here's the agreed commercial summary we will reflect in the term sheet to be routed to DocuSign: 

- Term: 24 months.
- Committed pool: 12 A100-equivalent GPUs provisioned in us-west.
- Start & ramp: 50% capacity at contract execution; 75% by Day 60; 100% by Day 180. Legal will allow a one-time extension of up to 60 days beyond Day 180 for unforeseen infra constraints.
- Discount: 22% off hosted equivalent list pricing for the committed pool; final TCV may adjust +/- 2-3% depending on final sizing confirmation.
- Onboarding credit: $45,000, applied as invoice credits across months 1-3.
- SLA: Commitment to 99% throughput availability for the reserved pool (sample credit schedule included in term sheet). Default fallback: automatic routing to hosted service for overflow; any credit events processed per SLO appendix.
- Operational lead: ops needs 30 days to reserve physical capacity in us-west; effective start date should account for this.

Next steps: I'll upload the clean term sheet to DocuSign (link below) and mark it for execution once procurement signs off. If you want to accelerate the ramp to Day 90 in exchange for an additional 2% discount on TCV, we can include that as an optional clause.
